{{Short description|German physicist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=February 2024}}
'''Klaus Blaum''' (born 27 December 1971 in Sobernheim, now [[Bad Sobernheim]], Germany) is a German physicist and director at the [[Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics]] in [[Heidelberg]], Germany.

==Life and scientific work==
Blaum studied physics at the [[University of Mainz|Johannes Gutenberg-University Mainz]], Germany.<ref name="t012">{{cite web | title=75 aus 75: Klaus Blaum | website=Welcome to the Gutenberg-Netzwerk! | date=8 October 2024 | url=https://gutenberg-netzwerk.uni-mainz.de/projekte/75aus75/klausblaum/ | language=de | access-date=21 May 2025}}</ref> After his physics diploma in 1997 and several research visits at the [[Pacific Northwest National Laboratory]], Richland, Washington, US, he graduated in 2000 as Doctor rerum naturalium in physics.<ref name="x409">{{cite web | title=Klaus Blaum: Max-Planck-Institut für Kernphysik | website=Startseite | date=19 June 2005 | url=https://www.mpi-hd.mpg.de/mpi/de/forschung/abteilungen-und-gruppen/gespeicherte-und-gekuehlte-ionen/mitglieder/klaus-blaum | language=de | access-date=21 May 2025}}</ref> From 2000 to 2002 he was postdoctoral research associate of [[Gesellschaft für Schwerionenforschung|GSI Darmstadt]] (working group of [[H. Jürgen Kluge]]) and until 2004 Research Associate (CERN Fellow) at the European Organization for Nuclear Research [[CERN]], Geneva, Switzerland and Project Leader for "Mass spectrometry of exotic nuclides with [[ISOLTRAP]]" at ISOLDE.<ref name="x409" /> In October 2004 Klaus Blaum became Project Leader of the "Helmholtz Research Group for Young Investigators" on "Experiments with Stored and Cooled Ions" at the Johannes Gutenberg-University Mainz.<ref name="x409" /> In 2006 he habilitated in [[experimental physics]] at the University Mainz about ''High precision mass spectrometry with Penning traps and storage rings''.<ref name="x409" />

From 2004 to 2008 Blaum taught at the Johannes Gutenberg-University Mainz. His achievement was honored with the Teaching Award of Rheinland-Pfalz 2006.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hochschulevaluierungsverbund.de/preistraegerinnen-und-preistraeger-des-lehrpreises-des-landes-rheinland-pfalz/|title=Preisträgerinnen und Preisträger des Lehrpreises des Landes Rheinland-Pfalz &#124; Hochschulevaluierungsverbund Süd-West e.V.|website=www.hochschulevaluierungsverbund.de|access-date=26 November 2021}}</ref>
In October 2007 he was appointed as director and scientific member at the Max-Planck-Institute for Nuclear Physics in Heidelberg, Germany. Since April 2008 he is honorary professor (W3) at the [[University of Heidelberg|Ruprecht-Karls-University Heidelberg]], Germany.<ref name="x409" /> In November 2008 he was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (APS). After his first term (2012–2014), he was again vice chairman of the advisory committee "Hadrons and Nuclei" of the [[Federal Ministry of Education and Research (Germany)|Federal Ministry of Education and Research]] (BMBF) from 2018 to March 2020. During the membership period 2012–2019 Klaus Blaum was a member of the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft|DFG]] (German Research Foundation) Review Board 308 "Optics, [[Quantum optics|Quantum Optics]] and Physics of Atoms, Molecules and Plasmas". From June 2016 to December 2019 he was deputy chairman of the FAIR/GSI Joint Scientific Council, chairman of the Scientific Committee of GSI and member of the supervisory board of GSI. From July 2020 to June 2023, Klaus Blaum was vice president of the [[Max Planck Society]] and responsible for the Institutes of the Chemistry, Physics and Technology Section.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mpg.de/15105526/new-vice-presidents|title=New team, new ideas|website=www.mpg.de|access-date=26 November 2021}}</ref>

==Main research areas==
His scientific work focuses on precision experiments with stored and cooled ions as well as the investigation of fundamental processes of molecular ions. Another main research field is the development of novel storage, cooling and detection techniques for future experiments.
